item.description: Ahmed Haroun, a senior security official during the rule of longtime dictator Omar al-Bashir, and later chairman of the former ruling National Congress Party, was detained in Omdurman, the sister city of the capital, Khartoum, according to two lawyers on his defense team. item.title: Africanews: ‘We are left with silence’: Egypt’s press freedom under threat
item.description: Egypt's latest prosecution of journalists attempts to "silence" the last surviving vestiges of the free press, Lina Attalah, head of preeminent outlet Mada Masr, told AFP days before she faces jail time in court.

item.title: Africanews: Ancient meets modern as art exhibition opens at Egypt's pyramids
item.description: The sixth edition of the ‘Forever Is Now’ art exhibition is set against the Pyramids of Giza. The Egyptian landscape and its ancient monuments are more than just a backdrop, they also provide the works’ conceptual anchor, creating a dialogue between past and present.

item.title: Africanews: Iranian citizens expect Israel’s Iran policy to remain unchanged
item.description: Iranians see no prospects of change to Israel's policy over Tehran even under a new Israeli government.

item.title: Africanews: South Africa's ANC faces coalition talks after local election losses
item.description: The African National Congress came in first place in South Africa's local elections but suffered its worst-ever electoral setback, according to final results on Sunday.

item.title: Africanews: Egypt train crash: Survivors describe horror after collision kills seven
item.description: Seven people were killed and at least 125 others injured when two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, the Chief Prosecutor’s office said in a statement

item.title: Africanews: Gambia opposition leader Bensouda seeks presidency amid abuse allegations
item.description: Supporters of Gambia’s UNITE-led coalition celebrated on Friday as their party leader Talib Ahmed Bensouda filed his candidacy papers for next month’s presidential election. The move comes despite a government report last week accusing the popular former mayor of financial improprieties.

item.title: Africanews: Somalia faces political turmoil after court rejects president's term extension
item.description: Somalia's political crisis is deepening, with the opposition accusing the president of sending troops to arrest the Supreme Court's chief justice after the tribunal declared an extension of his term "unlawful".

item.title: Africanews: Tanzania opposition hails Tundu Lissu's acquittal on treason charge
item.description: Tanzania's main opposition Chadema party celebrated a "victorious day" on Friday, after a court found their leader Tundu Lissu not guilty of treason.

item.title: Africanews: Senegal: Dakar surf school helps young Africans reclaim the waves
item.description: On the beaches of Dakar, a surf school is making the waves accessible to local children. Founder Ibra Samb, who learnt to surf on plywood, hopes to inspire a new generation.

item.description: The African National Congress, which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, took 30.76 percent of votes in municipal elections, its worst-ever electoral performance, the electoral commission said Sunday

item.title: Africanews: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV welcomed by Javier Milei for historic visit
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Argentina, on Sunday 8 November, for the first papal visit to the country in nearly 40 years. President Javier Milei welcomed him at Buenos Aires airport, while the city's iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honour.

item.title: BBC Africa: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
item.description: For some tourists, the contrast between Somalia's reputation and what they experience on the ground can be striking.

item.title: Africanews: Netherlands: Sea of red fills Amsterdam streets in Gaza protest
item.description: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam in the Netherlands on Sunday 8 November, demanding that the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over the war in Gaza.

item.title: Africanews: Poland: Kraków mourns six victims as shooting site reopens
item.description: Kraków's historic main square in southern Poland reopened to the public on Sunday 8 November, just over 24 hours after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 15 others injured. Residents are lighting candles in memory of the victims, while bullet marks remain visible on café windows.

item.title: BBC Africa: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
item.description: Several carriages derailed after two trains travelling in the same direction crashed outside the city of Giza.

item.title: BBC Africa: South Africa's ANC records worst-ever results in local elections
item.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa says the verdict must be respected, while the party's secretary-general calls the outcome "catastrophic".

item.title: BBC Africa: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa
item.description: After losing her sight in 2009, Nigeria’s Rukayat Suleimon has overcome isolation and limited support to make history as the first blind woman to win gold at the World Sambo Cup.

item.description: The African National Congress came in first place in South Africa's local elections but suffered its worst-ever electoral setback, according to final results on Sunday.

item.title: BBC Africa: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
item.description: It is yet unclear what caused the accident but Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation is underway and will "hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence".

item.title: Africanews: Egypt: 4 dead and dozens injured after two trains collide south of Cairo
item.description: Four people are dead and dozens injured after two trains collided south of Cairo on Sunday. Egypt’s railway authority said a train traveling to Giza from Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan.
